name: Dual Landmine Standing Chest Press
description: The dual landmine standing chest press uses two barbells anchored side by side to perform a bilateral pressing motion that mimics the arc of a dumbbell press with the stability benefits of a fixed load path. Standing during the press increases core and hip engagement, making it both a chest and full-body stability exercise.

execution.starting_position: Set up two landmine attachments side by side. Hold the free end of each barbell at chest height, standing with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Anchor two barbells in adjacent landmine sleeves. Load equal weight on each. Stand close enough to hold both bar ends at chest height simultaneously without awkward angles.
steps: Step 1: Hold both bar ends at chest height with palms facing inward.
Step 2: Press both bars forward and slightly upward simultaneously, extending the arms.
Step 3: At full extension, attempt to squeeze the hands toward each other to increase pectoral contraction.
Step 4: Slowly lower both bars back to the chest in a controlled arc.
Step 5: Maintain a neutral spine and braced core throughout all reps.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you press forward. Inhale as you lower the bars back to the chest.
common_mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare far out to the sides
Using momentum or leg drive to help each rep
Letting the lower back arch excessively
safety_considerations: Ensure both landmine sleeves are secure and the barbells are equally loaded
Start with the bars unloaded to learn the motion
Have a spotter available when using heavier loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Press until both arms are fully extended. Lower until hands return to chest level, keeping the bar ends together as much as possible.
coaching_cues: Press the bars in converging arcs
Squeeze the chest at the top
Keep the belly tight and ribs down
